title: Pressure, Winds, Storms and Cyclones
seo_title: Pressure, Winds, Storms and Cyclones Class 8 Science Worksheet (NCERT Curiosity Ch 6)
standard_code: Class 8, Curiosity Chapter 6: Pressure, Winds, Storms and Cyclones
standard_text: Pressure as force per unit area; pressure in liquids and its increase with depth; atmospheric pressure; air moving from high to low pressure; winds, monsoons, thunderstorms and cyclones; weather instruments and safety during storms (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 6).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 8 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 6: pressure = force ÷ area, pressure in liquids, atmospheric pressure, winds from high to low pressure, thunderstorms, cyclones and safety. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Wind blows from high pressure to low pressure.
body_html:
How to think about it

Pressure is the force acting on a unit area: pressure = force ÷ area, measured in pascals (N/m²). The same force on a smaller area gives more pressure, which is why knives are sharp and bag straps are wide. Liquid pressure increases with depth, so dams are thicker at the bottom. Air also exerts pressure, which falls as we go higher.

Warm air rises, leaving low pressure, and wind blows from high pressure to low pressure. Uneven heating of land and sea brings the monsoon. A cyclone is a huge storm spinning around a low-pressure eye; the IMD gives warnings, and people should move to safe shelters.

Example

100 N on 0.5 m²?

P = F ÷ A

Answer: 200 Pa

Example

Which hole spurts water farthest?

pressure increases with depth

Answer: the lowest hole

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a larger area gives more pressure.
  • Saying wind blows from low to high pressure.
  • Watching a cyclone from the beach.

items.q: A force of 400 N acts on an area of 2 m². What is the pressure?
items.e: Pressure = force ÷ area = 400 ÷ 2 = 200 Pa.

items.q: A force of 500 N acts on an area of 2 m². What is the pressure?
items.e: Pressure = force ÷ area = 500 ÷ 2 = 250 Pa.

items.q: A tin of paint weighing 80 N can rest on a face of area 0.01 m² or 0.02 m². On which face does it exert more pressure on the floor?
c: the same pressure on both faces
items.e: The same force on a smaller area gives a larger pressure: 80 ÷ 0.01 = 8,000 Pa.

items.q: What is a thunderstorm?

items.q: Why is the wall of a dam thicker at the bottom?
